author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Faith-based childcare programs are helping cover gaps in New Hampshire’s limited care network, but recent changes show how closely their futures can be tied to the churches that house them. Emmanuel Child Care Center in Rochester closed Aug. 28 after 37 years when Emmanuel Church decided to use the space for an expanding food pantry.

Other church-based providers are growing. Kids by the Common, located at Londonderry Presbyterian Church, expanded from two classrooms to six in 2024 and increased enrollment from 27 children to 62 in about a year and a half. The program offers infant, toddler and preschool care and had long provided full-day kindergarten before Londonderry public schools began offering it this year.

Little Blessings in Northwood rents space from St. Joseph’s Catholic Church and teaches a nondenominational Christian curriculum. Its operator said enrollment fell after the church opened a prekindergarten-through-eighth-grade school in the same building. Both Little Blessings and Kids by the Common are state licensed, accept state childcare assistance and follow state early-learning standards. Their different trajectories illustrate both the access these programs provide and the operational uncertainty that can accompany shared religious facilities and thin childcare margins.
dek: Church-based providers are expanding care in some communities while closures and shared-building changes expose operational risks.
headline: Faith-based childcare programs navigate growth and closures in New Hampshire
